messages:
lia (oncall): paging: seeing a spike of 5xxs in EU canary, traffic split looks wrong (should be 5% -> looks ~40%). creating thread to coord :rotating_light:
jamie (eng-sre): seeing same in dashboards — EU edge -> green cluster has elevated 502/524, but green instances are healthy per /healthz
sophie (eng-runtime): suspect routing mismatch at global router or DNS not honoring weight for the canary. logs show many requests routed to eu-green-backend-1
edge-monitor-bot: alert: eu-canary-5xx-rate > 8% for 3m. current 5xx: 12.4% | traffic_split_green: 42% | expected_green: 5%
lia (oncall): @deploy-bot can you show last deploy for eu green?
deploy-bot: last deploy: revision r2026.03.15-53 to eu-west-1-green at 2026-03-15T02:01Z by @sophie. canary config applied: weight=5, header-based routing disabled, DNS weight-based routing enabled.
maria (support): we have ~7 customer reports (low-latency errors) in EU region, ticket IDs: #9241 #9242 #9247 — marking potential customer impact
kevin (product): flagging high priority for dashboards and any paying customers in EU. what's mitigation plan?
jamie (eng-sre): quick mitigation options: 1) kill feature flag for canary routing (force all traffic to blue) 2) rollback green deploy 3) cut DNS weight to 0 or remove green from LB. prefer minimal blast radius — recommend feature flag kill-switch first if available
sophie (eng-runtime): feature flag exists but old rollout used DNS weight — flagging that kill-switch only affects router header path, not DNS weight. DNS-based canary is controlled in infra service 'global-router' config.
lia (oncall): ok do we have a one-liner to force all traffic back to blue via global-router?
sophie (eng-runtime): run: ```global-routerctl set-weight eu-west-1 green 0``` that will drop weight to 0 and rebalance to blue. it propagates within ~15s to router.
jamie (eng-sre): checking DNS metrics — TTL for canary records was set to 300. but many edges cache longer due to CDN. that could explain slow convergence and >5% traffic to green. need immediate router-level change
lia (oncall): executing router weight change now, will report back. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
lia (oncall): ran: `global-routerctl set-weight eu-west-1 green 0` — CLI returned success. watching metrics.
edge-monitor-bot: router-change: weight eu-west-1 green -> 0 requested by lia at 02:07:12Z
jamie (eng-sre): metrics: green traffic dropping from 42% -> 9% in ~40s. 5xx rate decreasing in EU from 12.4% -> 3.6%
maria (support): customer reports dropping off, tickets #9241/#9242 updated to 'mitigated' — letting customers know we're working on root cause
kevin (product): good, can we keep canary disabled until blameless postmortem? prefer safety.
sophie (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll pause the canary rollout and create a follow-up to check the deploy artifact. rollback not needed since weight is 0 but we should ensure the green revision isn't auto-promoted.
lia (oncall): leaving thread in monitoring state. can someone confirm whether the DNS weight config was supposed to be used? who set that for this deploy?
sophie (eng-runtime): it was part of the deploy manifest — the deploy smoke test team historically flips weight via global-router. this time the manifest included both DNS and router weight, but router was meant to be authoritative. however I see in the deploy logs that the router update failed once and retry happened, while DNS update succeeded — looks like a race condition.
jamie (eng-sre): logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:00:59Z deploymgr: applying manifest r2026.03.15-53
2026-03-15T02:01:01Z deploymgr: update global-router weight -> success
2026-03-15T02:01:02Z deploymgr: update dns weight -> success
2026-03-15T02:01:03Z global-router: update failed (timeout) retrying
2026-03-15T02:01:05Z global-router: update success
```
jamie (eng-sre): so ordering made DNS take effect before router finished applying, meaning some edge nodes followed DNS and sent traffic to green while router was still inconsistent. combined with long CDN caching TTL it caused a partial rollout spike.
kevin (product): do we know customer count impacted / which customers?
maria (support): tickets came from EU customers in region eu-west-1 and one multi-region customer who hits EU edge. all reported transient 5xx. no data loss reported. marking 'incident severity: S2' for now but will escalate if more reports come in.
lia (oncall): next steps: 1) keep green weight 0 2) pause auto-promote for this artifact 3) reduce DNS TTL to 60 (to help future fixes) 4) postmortem and change deployment ordering to apply router then DNS or use atomic update. assigning owners: sophie -> pause/policy, jamie -> DNS TTL + monitoring, sophie + deploy team -> deploy ordering fix
sophie (eng-runtime): I've paused auto-promote and created a ticket: INF-4387. will open PR to switch ordering in deploymgr to 'router then dns' and add a retry/verify step.
jamie (eng-sre): changing DNS TTL now: `dnsctl set-ttl eu-canary 60` — command returned success. watching edge caches — should see faster convergence on next update.
lia (oncall): metrics look stable. 5xx back to baseline ~0.6% EU. green traffic steady <1%.
kevin (product): thank you everyone. I'll inform ops leads and prepare a short customer note if anything changes.
maria (support): closing immediate tickets as 'mitigated' and will follow up if users reopen.
lia (oncall): I'll hand this to oncall rotation for postmortem (next oncall: jamie). leaving channel but will stay on pager for 30m.
jamie (eng-sre): ack taking postmortem lead. will schedule blameless review and include timeline + deploymgr fix.
incident-bot: incident: INF-2026-03-15-003 created, severity S2, alerting timeline logged.
sophie (eng-runtime): quick note for postmortem: include reproducer steps, deploymgr logs, and CDN cache behaviour. also check if any other regions used DNS-only canary.
lia (oncall): thanks all — closing incident thread for active mitigation. further discussion will go to #postmortems/infra once jamie opens the doc. :white_check_mark:
